Dong Nguyen released Flappy Bird in 2013; its viral difficulty redefined casual games for touch screens.
Snake became world-famous on the Nokia 6110 in 1997, proving phones could be gaming platforms.
Atari released Breakout in 1976 as an evolution of Pong; its development inspired Steve Wozniak to create an ultra-efficient board.
The modern memory card game was marketed as Concentration in 1959, adapting a traditional children\'s pastime.
Minesweeper came with Windows in 1990 to teach mouse usage, becoming an office addiction worldwide.
In 1952, the OXO project at Cambridge University brought Tic-Tac-Toe to a computer, one of the first video games with graphics.
The sliding puzzle 15 Puzzle sparked a craze in 1874, challenging players to arrange tiles by moving only the empty space.
The 1894 dictionary already described Hangman as a popular school game, decades before it appeared in children\'s books.
Gabriele Cirulli created 2048 in 2014 as an open source experiment; within days it became a global logic puzzle phenomenon.
Howard Garns popularized Sudoku in 1979 under the name Number Place, before Japan renamed and exported it worldwide.
